input: It should be noted that, once the corrosion allowance has been taken into account, the wall thickness for the absorber is 27 mm. This is the figure that should be carried forward, rather than any earlier thickness that might have been considered before the allowance was added. Turning then to the gaskets, the excerpt compares two possible gasket materials, although it does so on a deliberately narrow basis, namely temperature limit only. On that basis, the higher-rated material is the one that is preferred. No other property is introduced into the comparison, and the preference should not be read as if it were based on a broader assessment than the one actually stated. The wall-thickness decision and the gasket decision are related in the sense that they appear in the same part of the report, but they are nevertheless distinct points. One concerns the absorber wall after the corrosion allowance; the other concerns which gasket material has the higher temperature limit. The lean solvent pump is part of the wider equipment context for the absorber, although the excerpt does not use the pump as a reason to change either the stated thickness or the criterion used for the gaskets. Similarly, $\Delta P$ and NPSH appear as terms that are already in play in the surrounding discussion, and the excerpt simply continues to use them rather than pausing to explain them again. The discussion therefore remains focused on the 27 mm wall thickness and on the temperature-limit comparison between the two gasket materials, with the higher-rated option being preferred
